Font choice.

  • For your four year old's birthday invitations, comic sans is okay.
  • For anything business related--such as a resume, company-wide memo, business letter, et cetera--use Calibri or Times New Roman.
  • When you indent an entire paragraph because it's a quote, you can do it in a monospaced font. You don't have to, but sometimes it adds a nice touch. Don't use Courier New, though. Use Consolas. It's leagues better.
  • Use papyrus when you want a swift slap to the face.
  • Impact is okay for small amounts of text in large font, such as captioning memes, on billboards, or in rare occasions as a header. Don't use it in anything professional. Never write more than one sentence in it on the same document. That one sentence must always be centered and above all other text.

Font is a powerful thing. It changes the way people read your document, and changes the mood of it extremely. Use the right fonts in the right scenario, and your document will look good. Use a font in the wrong scenario, and your document isn't enjoyable to read, looks sloppy, and doesn't get your message out effectively.
